meta.title: LedgerLine — Q3 2026 board update
meta.description: Board update for a real-time marketplace payouts company: answer first, KPI scorecard, volume trend, a win, a margin miss and its fix, cash, Q4 roadmap, risks and three asks.

slides.heading: Volume beat plan by 8%. Margin slipped three points.
slides.lead: We moved $4.1B to sellers in Q3. Two votes today win the margin back by January.
slides.notes: Lead with both halves of the answer. The board will ask about margin first, so do not bury it.

slides.heading: Gig platforms drove volume, card fees cut margin, and FedNow is the fix
slides.body:
Won: payout volume $4.1B, 8% over plan.
Won: 214 live marketplaces, 14 over plan.
Missed: gross margin 61% against a 64% plan.
slides.aside: Decide today: fund the $1.2M FedNow build, and add a second sponsor bank.

slides.heading: Four of five KPIs beat plan; gross margin is the exception
Quarterly payout volume grew 2.6× in a year to $4.1B
slides.lead: Source: LedgerLine ledger, settled payouts only, close of 2 October 2026.

slides.heading: What worked, and what did not
Instant-to-debit payouts won gig platforms and 61% of new volume
slides.body: We launched instant payouts to debit cards in June. Gig platforms pay drivers and couriers daily, so they moved first: 23 signed in the quarter.
slides.aside: $0.49B of $0.8B new quarterly volume came from gig platforms. Median time to cash: 38 seconds.

slides.heading: Gross margin fell 3 points when card-network fees rose 40%
slides.left:
Card push fee held at $0.18.
30% of payouts sent to cards.
Gross margin 64%.
slides.right:
Fee rose to $0.25 on 1 July.
44% of payouts went to cards.
Gross margin 61%. Fix: send bank payouts on FedNow at $0.045.
slides.notes: Say it plainly: we priced instant payouts on the old fee. FedNow moves bank-account payouts off cards and recovers the margin.

slides.heading: Cash covers 34 months at today's burn

stats.label: Runway at current burn, up from 30 in Q2

slides.heading: Q4 moves bank payouts to FedNow and margin back to 64%
One sponsor bank holding every dollar is now the top risk
We ask the board for two votes and one piece of advice

cards.title: Vote: $1.2M for FedNow
cards.body: Six engineers for two quarters. Pays back in 5 months.

cards.title: Vote: second sponsor bank
cards.body: Crestline Bank term sheet, $0.3M a year.

cards.title: Advice: UK timing
cards.body: File the EMI licence now, or after FedNow ships?

slides.notes: Take the FedNow vote first; the bank vote depends on it. The UK question is advice, not a vote.

slides.heading: Fund FedNow and a second bank to win margin back by January
slides.lead: Both votes today let the pilot start on 14 October.
